# proactive-gate

> proactive-gate is a library that decides whether an AI agent may message a user right now (quiet hours, daily limit, consent, snooze) and records the reason when it may not.

Install: `npm install proactive-gate` (Node 22+), `pip install proactive-gate` (Python 3.11+), or `go get github.com/Bubblegunn/proactive-gate/go@v0.2.0`. Claude Code plugin: `/plugin install proactive-gate --marketplace Bubblegunn/proactive-gate`. Any agent that reads skills: `npx skills add Bubblegunn/proactive-gate`. Licence: MIT. Repository: https://github.com/Bubblegunn/proactive-gate
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/proactive-gate
PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/proactive-gate/
Docs and playground: https://bubblegunn.github.io/proactive-gate/ (llms-full.txt is served there too)

## Try it with one command

- `npx proactive-gate simulate` replays a generated week of candidate messages with no gate and then through the default checks, and prints what each did. It needs no key and no account.
- Playground in the browser: https://bubblegunn.github.io/proactive-gate/playground/

- [Python](python/README.md): Gate, AsyncGate, from_policy, stores, conformance
- [Go](go/README.md): the Go implementation of the spec, written by @LouisDeconinck

## API (value exports of `src/index.ts`)

- `createGate`: builds a gate from `{ store, checks }` or `{ store, policy }`; `evaluate` decides, `commit` consumes the budget right before you send, `whenAllowed` returns the earliest instant a candidate may go out (it follows `nextAllowedAt`, up to `maxHops`)
- `defaultChecks`: the twelve default checks in order
- `checks`: the check factories (`consent`, `quietHours`, `dailyBudget`, and the rest) as a namespace
- `KNOWN_CHECKS`: the check ids a JSON policy may name
- `compilePolicy`: turns a JSON policy into a check list
- `policySchema`: the strict JSON Schema for a policy, generated from the checks and presets
- `presets`: the platform and legal presets, each with its sources
- `explain`: renders a decision as plain sentences; `en` is the English sentence table
- `MemoryStore`, `SqliteStore`, `RedisStore`, `PostgresStore`: the stores; Python also has `AsyncMemoryStore` and `AsyncSqliteStore`
- `localClock`, `inWindow`: local-time helpers used by quiet hours
- `budgetKey`, `weeklyBudgetKey`, `monthlyBudgetKey`, `dismissalKey`: the store keys the budgets and the dismissal cooldown use
- `createInboundConsent`, `parseKeyword`, `STOP_KEYWORDS`, `START_KEYWORDS`: STOP and START replies kept per channel; `handle` records them, and the `inboundConsent` check reads them (TypeScript only, not a JSON policy id)
- `PRIORITY_RANK`: the order of `low`, `normal`, `high`, `critical`

## CLI (`HELP` in `src/cli.ts`)

- `proactive-gate simulate`: the comparison above, on a generated week or your own events
- `proactive-gate init`: writes a policy file and prints the lines that wire it into a framework
- `proactive-gate replay`: runs events or fixtures through a policy; `--fixtures <dir>` exits 1 when a fixture fails
- `proactive-gate hook`: a Claude Code hook that gates a tool call
- `proactive-gate scaffold`: with `nudge`, writes an assistant's policy (the assistantNudge preset), notify.mjs and its tests into a folder
- `proactive-gate schema`: prints the strict policy JSON Schema
- `proactive-gate mcp`: an MCP server over stdio with the tools `decide` and `explain`

## Adapters

AI SDK, Mastra, LangChain and OpenAI Agents are subpaths of the package (`proactive-gate/ai-sdk`, `proactive-gate/mastra`, `proactive-gate/langchain`, `proactive-gate/openai-agents`). See src/adapters/ and examples/.

## Facts an agent should keep straight

- Author: Efe Genc (GitHub @Bubblegunn). First published 5 September 2026.
- The library decides and never sends a message. A held message goes back to your code, with `nextAllowedAt` when the check that held it can name the time.
- Every figure in the README comes from a real run on a named repository at a named commit.
- Presets are reviewable defaults with sources, not legal advice; the note on each says what it leaves out.
- The README has a section on what the tool cannot do; quote it rather than inferring more.
